summary: A circular queue stores its elements in a fixed array and wraps indices around with modulo arithmetic, so freed slots at the front are reused. Both enqueue and dequeue are O(1) with no wasted space.

sections.heading: Why circular
sections.body: A linear array queue marches rightward and abandons the left part. Treating the array as a ring means that after the last index you continue at index 0, so capacity is always fully usable.

sections.heading: Core formulas
sections.code:
rear        = (front + size - 1) % capacity   // last element
next_free   = (front + size) % capacity       // where enqueue writes
after dequeue: front = (front + 1) % capacity

sections.heading: Operations
bullets: enqueue: if size == capacity, report full; else write at next_free, size++.
dequeue: if size == 0, report empty; else read a[front], front = (front+1) % capacity, size--.

sections.heading: Full versus empty
sections.body: If you track only `front` and `rear`, a full queue and an empty one look identical (front == rear). Three standard fixes: keep a `size` counter (above), leave one slot permanently unused, or keep a separate full/empty flag.

subtopics.title: Power-of-two capacity
subtopics.summary: Replace modulo with a bit mask.

sections.body: If capacity is 2^k, `i % cap` equals `i & (cap - 1)`, which is faster and lets head and tail run as free-running unsigned counters. This is the layout of the Linux kernel's `kfifo`.

bullets: Logging buffers that overwrite the oldest entry.

sections.body: When full, advance `front` as you write so the oldest item is dropped. Useful for telemetry windows and crash logs.
With one writer and one reader, the writer only updates `tail` and the reader only `head`, so a ring buffer needs no locks, just correct memory ordering.
With front, size, and capacity: the front element is `a[front]`; the rear element is `a[(front + size - 1) % capacity]`. Return a sentinel or error when size is 0.
sections.code:
int get_front(const Q *q) { return q->size ? q->a[q->front] : -1; }
int get_rear(const Q *q)  { return q->size ? q->a[(q->front + q->size - 1) % q->cap] : -1; }

takeaways: Indices wrap with `% capacity`, reusing freed slots.
enqueue and dequeue are O(1); no shifting.
Distinguish full from empty with a size counter or a spare slot.
Power-of-two capacities allow a fast mask instead of modulo.

practice.title: Moving average from a data stream
Implement without a size counter using one spare slot
